grok.rationale: At closing the REIT Member contributed its ownership interests in six grocery-anchored shopping centers (the Initial Properties, ~$94.3M) into the newly formed Joint Venture, so the customer-facing product assets crossed the ownership boundary (T4). Simultaneously the Joint Venture entered a separate Master Property Management, Leasing and Construction Management Agreement under which Phillips Edison & Company Ltd.—explicitly ‘not the new venture as an in-house operating capability’—retained day-to-day management, operation and maintenance of those same properties, documenting a product-vs-process structural mismatch at closing (gap_45=1). Operational processes and the people/organization that run them both remained with Phillips Edison affiliates (Property Manager plus PECO Member as JV manager), so T5 and T6 stayed aligned and gap_56=0; the Master Property Management agreement (together with the advisory-fee reallocation amendments) contractually allocated that shared substrate at closing (gap_mitigated=yes).

openai.rationale: The REIT Member contributed six shopping-center properties to the Joint Venture, while day-to-day management, operation, and maintenance remained with Phillips Edison & Company Ltd. under a separate Master Property Management, Leasing and Construction Management Agreement. This documents a product-versus-process ownership mismatch at closing that was contractually absorbed through the management agreement and related fee-allocation amendments. No gap_56 is documented because the retained operating processes and the organization running them remained together with the same Phillips Edison manager under that agreement.
